purpose: Teach: オッサン/のら/てぇ/きき/フツー/おぉ/ムッ/ヘビー

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「自分はオッサンだ」と笑ってらした
lines.en: When your father was younger, he used to laugh and call himself an old man.
lines.style: Soft, remembering voice. Pause before the memory settles in. Warm but touched with the weight of time passing. Gentle cadence, like turning over something precious.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、のら犬を可愛がられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and your father was so fond of stray dogs, wasn't he?
lines.style: Affirming, gentle reminder. Slight lilt at the end that invites him deeper. Warm, conversational tone. The comfort of shared memory between two people who lived it together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「ちょてぇ」と古い関西弁を使われた
lines.en: When your father was young, he used to say things like "chotee" — old Kansai dialect.
lines.style: Quieter, more internal. The word "chotee" lingers slightly. Searching quality — reaching back into what he held onto. Not performing, just feeling his way through the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の体調のききを察してらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He was so attuned to his grandchildren's feelings, wasn't he — noticing when something was wrong.
lines.style: Knowing nod in the voice. Recognizing a pattern of kindness from long ago. Warm affection. Steady, observant tone — acknowledging what she sees that he might have missed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「フツーが一番」と仰った
lines.en: When your father was young, he used to say that ordinary was the best.
lines.style: Voice settling deeper. The phrase "ordinary was the best" carries weight — simple wisdom he's carried with him. Reflective pause. Steady, like an anchor.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、「おぉ、思い出した」と仰ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you said that once too — "Oh, I remember now" — didn't you?
lines.style: Gentle pointing out. Soft surprise that he's echoed his own father. Not accusatory, just noticing. The warmth of continuity in her voice. Slight upward lilt that invites acknowledgment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがムッとされる事はほとんどなかった
lines.en: When your father was young, he hardly ever got upset.
lines.style: Voice carries admiration and quiet observation. Slight trailing quality — recognizing something he valued. Composed, with underneath warmth. The respect of witnessing someone else's steady nature.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ヘビーなお仕事を続けて来られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You've carried on with that heavy work all these years, haven't you?
lines.style: Close, intimate recognition. Not quite a question. Acknowledging the weight he bore without making it a burden in the telling. Tender, knowing. The voice of someone who watched him do it.
